journey.title: Type a check-in date, then Tab to the guests field
journey.goal: After typing a date and pressing Tab, focus stays on the next field so the user can keep filling the form

functionalJourney.title: Pick a check-in day with the pointer
functionalJourney.goal: Clicking a day fills the check-in date and the guests field still takes input

guards.title: Paging months with the pointer keeps keyboard focus in the date field
guards.goal: After clicking Next month, focus is back in the date field so arrow keys and typing keep working

plan.root_cause: The datepicker’s _onKeyChange handler lacks an explicit case for the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the picker is visible, the handler does not consume the key, but the blur event triggered by the focus change schedules a hide that, due to a race condition, refocuses the field before the blur completes, causing focus to remain on the check‑in field.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 that simply breaks, ensuring the keydown handler terminates early and does not interfere with the browser’s default focus‑moving action.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab after entering a date will move focus to the next focusable element (the guests field), allowing keyboard‑only users to continue filling the form without interruption.
functional_risks: Adding a explicit Tab case could interfere with any custom implementation that expects Tab to trigger datepicker behavior, but the datepicker does not assign any meaning to Tab, so risk is low.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid date in the check‑in field and pressing Tab, the active element must be the guests input.
Arrow keys (←, ↑, →, ↓) must still adjust the date when the picker is open.
Enter and Escape keys must still blur the field when the picker is open.
The picker should still hide appropriately when clicking outside or selecting a date.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's keydown handler (_onKeyChange) lacks a case for the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the picker is visible, the handler does not consume the key, but the blur event triggered by the focus change schedules a hide that, due to a race condition, refocuses the field before the blur completes, causing focus to remain on the check-in field. Additionally, the blur handler (_onInputBlur) unconditionally hides the picker when the field loses focus, even when the user is tabbing to the next field, which can cause a refocus via the picker's draw cycle.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 in _onKeyChange that sets a flag indicating Tab was pressed. In _onInputBlur, check this flag and skip hiding the picker when Tab was the cause of the blur. Clear the flag after a short timeout to avoid interfering with other blur events.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab after entering a date will move focus to the next focusable element (the guests field) without the datepicker interfering, allowing keyboard-only users to continue filling the form without interruption.
functional_risks: The flag-based approach adds a small amount of state to the picker instance, but it is scoped to the constructor and cleared quickly, so risk of leakage is low.
If the user tabs away and the picker stays visible momentarily, it will hide on the next blur or click outside, which is acceptable.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid date in the check-in field and pressing Tab, the active element must be the guests input.
Arrow keys (←, ↑, →, ↓) must still adjust the date when the picker is open.
Enter and Escape keys must still blur the field when the picker is open.
The picker should still hide appropriately when clicking outside or selecting a date.

plan.root_cause: The datepicker's _onKeyChange handler lacks a case for the Tab key (keyCode 9). When the picker is visible, pressing Tab does not close the picker. The blur handler (_onInputBlur) does not hide the picker on the first blur because of the _c flag, so the picker remains open. The picker's focusable buttons then trap focus, but the observed focus stays on the input due to a refocus in the picker's draw cycle.
plan.repair_strategy: Add a case for keyCode 9 in _onKeyChange that calls self.hide() to close the picker immediately, then allows the browser's default Tab behavior to move focus to the next field. This ensures the picker is hidden before the blur handler runs, preventing any interference.
plan.expected_accessibility_effect: Pressing Tab after entering a date in the check-in field will close the datepicker and move focus to the next focusable element (the guests field), allowing keyboard-only users to continue filling the form without interruption.
functional_risks: Calling hide() on Tab keydown may close the picker slightly earlier than the blur handler would, but this is consistent with user expectation that Tab moves to the next field.
If the picker is not visible, the Tab case is not triggered (since it's inside the isVisible() check), so no risk there.
verification_requirements: After typing a valid date in the check-in field and pressing Tab, the active element must be the guests input.
Arrow keys (←, ↑, →, ↓) must still adjust the date when the picker is open.
Enter and Escape keys must still blur the field when the picker is open.
The picker should still hide appropriately when clicking outside or selecting a date.
